cells.quote: All 3 calibrations of the WGS (µ=30, µ=50, and µ=70) detected a significant interaction effect between teaching format and learning disposition in the empirical dataset (Figure 3).

O.outcome_detail: Detection of a teaching-format by learning-disposition interaction in the simulated dataset

cells.quote: In the simulated dataset, no significant interaction between teaching format and learning disposition was observed when learning gains were calculated using the WGS, regardless of the µ-value applied (F1,996=0.39; P=.53; partial η²<0.001; Figure 3). Similarly, RLG did not reveal any significant difference in performance between the groups (F1,996=1.10; P=.29; partial η²=0.001).
cells.note: The simulated teaching-format and learning-disposition variables were randomly assigned, and the nonsignificant result is coded ns because no equivalence test or adequate-power claim is reported.

O.outcome_detail: applicability for estimating learning gain in a very small illustrative dataset

cells.quote: The illustrative dataset demonstrates that the WGS yields interpretable results even with very small sample sizes. In contrast, Rasch model–based approaches typically require substantially larger samples to ensure stable estimation of item parameters and person abilities.
cells.note: The illustrative dataset was artificial; RLG was not applied because the authors stated that Rasch estimation requires larger samples.
